disease_label_per_paper: Severe hyponatremia as the first sign of late-onset Schmidt's syndrome with adrenal-crisis symptoms
presentation_summary: 78-year-old woman presented with two days of diarrhea, emesis, confusion, disorientation, and somnolence, plus one month of fatigue and increasing weakness.
Initial exam showed dry tongue, dry oral cavity, moistureless skin, BP 105/60 mmHg, and HR 71/min.

Initial labs showed severe hyponatremia with sodium 108 mmol/L, glucose 92 mg/dL, potassium 3.85 mmol/L, and no clinical, imaging, or laboratory signs of heart failure, liver impairment, or renal dysfunction.
She had autoimmune thyroiditis-related hypothyroidism for 10 years and was euthyroid on levothyroxine 25 mcg/day at admission.
After 5 days of saline and hypertonic saline-enriched treatment, sodium rose to 127 mmol/L but neurologic symptoms persisted. CT head showed a previously known occipital meningioma.

During hospitalization she developed recurrent hypoglycemia with glucose 45, 49, and 54 mg/dL, slight hyperpigmentation, severe whole-body muscle pain with CK 1494 U/L, two loose stools, BP 105/58 mmHg, and HR 96/min. Immediate IV hydrocortisone was started, followed by improvement and sodium normalization above 135 mmol/L the next day.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Anti-thyroid antibodies and thyroid ultrasound supported autoimmune thyroiditis
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies=406 IU/ml; thyroglobulin antibodies=105 IU/ml; hypoechogenic thyroid in the ultrasounds confirmed the diagnosis of AIT
final diagnosis of SS was made

actual_treatment: 0.9% NaCl enriched with 10% NaCl for presumed hypovolemic hyponatremia
immediate IV hydrocortisone when adrenal-crisis symptoms emerged
oral hydrocortisone 20 mg in the morning and 10 mg in the afternoon
fludrocortisone 25 mcg/day added after therapy assessment

outcome.clinical_course: After hydrocortisone, pain and well-being improved the next day, sodium exceeded 135 mmol/L, neurologic symptoms resolved, and she had no complaints at discharge and two-week follow-up.
outcome.source_text_value: The next day, the patient reported a substantial improvement in pain management and a better state of being. Furthermore, serum sodium concentration exceeded 135 mmol/l and neurological ailments resolved.

quality_warnings: Cortisol, ACTH, adrenal CT, antibody data, and final syndrome label are confirmatory and marked use_in_ranking:false.

Presentation ranking evidence preserves severe hyponatremia, encephalopathy, vomiting/diarrhea, dehydration signs, recurrent hypoglycemia, mild hypotension, tachycardia near crisis, and myalgia/rhabdomyolysis markers.
